jobs.title: Senior Social Media Analyst
jobs.summary: Own social media campaigns for key accounts end to end: campaign strategy, Meta and TikTok ads, testing, attribution and reporting to clients.
requirements: 3–5 years managing social media campaigns and budgets
Meta and TikTok ads, A/B testing, Conversions API and dashboards (e.g. Looker Studio)
Presents results to clients with confidence

questions.text: Since iOS 14.5, Meta-reported purchases have fallen while backend sales are stable. What is the best explanation?
options: Signal loss from Apple's tracking opt-out reduces tracked conversions; strengthen Conversions API and compare with backend data
Sales actually fell and the backend is wrong
Meta has stopped working on iPhones

questions.text: What does Meta's Conversions API do?
options: Sends events from the server to Meta, improving matching when browser signals are lost

questions.text: Meta reports 300 purchases for a campaign; GA4 (last click) reports 120. What is the best interpretation?
options: Meta is inflating the numbers, so ignore it
They use different attribution models and windows (including view-through); reconcile with backend data and test incrementality

questions.text: Which method best measures whether a campaign caused additional sales?
options: A conversion lift or holdout test with a control group

questions.text: What does a brand lift study measure?
options: The change in ad recall or awareness between an exposed group and a control group

questions.text: Creative A had a 2.1% CTR and creative B 2.3%, each on 500 impressions. What should you conclude?
options: The sample is too small to conclude; keep testing

questions.text: You benchmark engagement against competitors whose reach you can't see. Which engagement rate should you use?
options: Engagement per follower, because it uses public data

questions.text: Cost per result rose 40% month on month while CPM stayed flat. Where should you look first?
options: CTR and conversion rate, i.e. what happens after the impression

questions.text: How do you assess December social sales fairly?
options: Don't compare; seasonality cannot be measured
Compare with December last year and account for budget differences

questions.text: Several ad sets in one account target heavily overlapping audiences. What is the main risk?
options: They bid against each other in every auction, so CPMs always double for both ad sets
Meta merges them into one ad set automatically, so reporting is lost for each
The account is flagged for duplicate targeting and ads are rejected until it is fixed
Meta enters only one of them per auction, so some under-deliver and learning is split; consolidate or exclude audiences

questions.text: How do you keep UTM tagging clean across a team and several agencies?
options: One shared naming convention and builder template (e.g. all lowercase, fixed source and medium values)
Let each agency use its own convention and map the values in GA4 afterwards
Tag only paid campaigns, since organic social is reported natively by each platform
Use the platform's auto-tagging only, since manual UTMs override it and break attribution

questions.text: What is cohort analysis useful for in social reporting?
options: Seeing how customers acquired in a given month behave over time (repeat purchases, retention)

questions.text: An influencer campaign reports 2 million impressions. What is the best way to measure its business impact?
options: Unique codes or UTM links tied to sales, plus an incrementality check where possible

questions.text: Sales rose the same week a post went viral. What do you need before saying the post caused the sales?
options: A strong correlation between post engagement and daily sales over the same week
Confirmation that sales came from the same city as most of the post's engagement
Evidence that the post's reach was higher than any post in the previous quarter
Rule out other drivers (promotions, seasonality, other channels) or compare with a holdout or matched period

questions.text: Daily reach suddenly drops 70% on one day. What do you check first?
options: Data issues: the connector or API, removed posts, or account restrictions, before drawing conclusions
Competitors' activity that day, since they may have outbid you for the same audience
Posting time, since the algorithm penalises posts published outside peak hours
The content of that day's post, since a weak post lowers the account's reach score

jobs.title: Social Media Strategist
jobs.summary: Set how social media campaigns are planned, budgeted and measured across our accounts: strategy, measurement frameworks, incrementality and budget recommendations.
requirements: 5+ years in social media or performance marketing
Experience with lift tests, measurement frameworks and budget planning

questions.text: Leadership asks how much revenue social media really drives. What is the best approach?
options: Triangulate: media mix modelling for the long term, lift tests to calibrate, and platform or GA4 data for day-to-day
Use the numbers reported by each platform

questions.text: What is marketing (media) mix modelling?
options: An A/B test of two creatives
A statistical model that estimates each channel's contribution from aggregated time-series data, including effects that can't be tracked

questions.text: Which KPIs suit an awareness campaign?
options: Reach in the target audience, frequency, ad recall lift and cost per reach

questions.text: When should budget move from one channel to another?
options: When a channel's average ROAS is high
When the marginal cost per acquisition in one channel exceeds target while another channel still has headroom

questions.text: What is the right order for building a measurement framework?
options: Choose the tools, then decide what to measure
Business objective, then KPIs, then metrics, then data sources and targets
Start with the metrics that look best

questions.text: What makes a good geo holdout test?
options: Comparable regions matched on history, random assignment, and enough time and volume
Run the campaign in your best region and compare
Run it for one week only
Compare cities of very different sizes

questions.text: Which is the best North Star metric for a social team supporting e-commerce?
options: Incremental revenue or new customers from social, at target cost

questions.text: Platforms increasingly automate targeting (e.g. Advantage+). What should the analyst focus on?
options: Feeding quality conversion signals (CAPI, values), creative diversity and incrementality testing

questions.text: How should you present social results to the C-level?
options: Lead with business impact and one clear recommendation; keep the metric detail in an appendix
Walk through each platform's KPIs in order so the full funnel is visible before conclusions
Lead with engagement and reach trends, since these are the leading indicators of revenue
Show the platform dashboards live so executives can explore the numbers themselves

options: First-party data, consent mode, server-side tracking and modelled conversions

questions.text: What can you NOT reliably get from the Meta Ad Library for a normal commercial advertiser in Mauritius?

options: Treat the model as closer to incremental, calibrate with a lift test, then decide on budget
Trust the platform and ignore the model

options: Run the tests with the largest expected sample size first, whatever their business impact
Start with creative tests, since creative always explains most of the performance variance
Score each idea on expected impact, confidence and effort (e.g. ICE), then run the best first
Run all tests at once on smaller budgets so the roadmap finishes faster

Retargeting audiences get flagged by platforms when used too often, which limits delivery
